surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the interaction of sodium tert-butoxide (NaO tBu) and diethylphosphoramidate (DEPA) precursors. The NaO tBu precursor provides sodium species, while DEPA provides phosphorus and nitrogen. The reaction mechanism is similar to the LiO tBu-DEPA process, where the sodium source reacts with the phosphorus and nitrogen precursors to form the sodium phosphorus oxynitride (NaPON) film. The reaction is not self-limiting, leading to non-ideal ALD behavior.
evidence: The surface reactions involve the interaction of sodium tert-butoxide (NaO tBu) and diethylphosphoramidate (DEPA) precursors. The NaO tBu precursor provides sodium species, while DEPA provides phosphorus and nitrogen. The reaction mechanism is similar to the LiO tBu-DEPA process, where the sodium source reacts with the phosphorus and nitrogen precursors to form the sodium phosphorus oxynitride (NaPON) film. The reaction is not self-limiting, leading to non-ideal ALD behavior. The NaO tBu precursor is bulkier and less volatile than LiO tBu, which affects the reaction dynamics. The reaction of NaO tBu-DEPA may be more complex than the reactions of LiO tBu-DEPA and NaO tBu-H2O, requiring further studies aimed at understanding the surface mediated reaction chemistry.
